newsitem.title: UK: Philippines non-life insurance premiums rise 16%.
newsitem.headline: Philippines non-life insurance premiums rise 16%.

text.p: Nonlife insurance premiums in the Philippines grew 16% in 1995 to P9.58 billion from P8.26 billion in the previous year,accrdong to the national insurance Commission (IC) show.
The sector incurred losses of P4.74 billion in 1995, 18.8% higher than the previous year's P3.99 billion.
The loss ratio was 49.48% for the whole sector, the commission said.
Motor car insurance got the biggest share of the premiums with P4.85 billion. However, it also recorded the highest losses of P3.02 billion or a loss ratio of 62.3%.

Fire insurance earned total premiums of P2.04 billion and losses of P900 million, for a loss ratio of 44.1%. Marine insurance earned premiums of P870 million and losses of P29 million, for a loss ratio of 33.3%.

Business operations of nonlife insurance firms also did well in 1995 as consolidated net income rose 14.29% to P880 million from P770 million the previous year. Gross investment income and other income grew 18.4% to P1.48 billion from P1.25 billion.
Total taxes paid to the government by the sector also went up 21.6% to P450 million from P370 million.
Consolidated assets of the non-life sector grew 22.2% to P33.51 billion in 1995 from P27.42 billion in the previous year even as liabilities also grew 26% to P20.37 billion from P16.17 billion.

There are currently 100 authorized nonlife companies in the country, according to the IC. Of these, 10 are foreign professional reinsurers, three domestic professional reinsurers, and one composite insurance company.
The industry has 6,735 ordinary agents, 679 general agents, 101 insurance brokers, 42 reinsurance brokers, 59 accredited adjusters and 569 non-life company underwriters.

To date, only one foreign company has joined the nonlife business, MAPFRE International S.A. of Spain which started operations in February last year. Foreign nonlife insurance firms are wary of entering the sector because the country is too prone to national disasters, industry analysts say.
Two domestic nonlife companies, namely Petrogen Insurance Corp. and Ayala General Insurance Corp., were licensed in November 1996 and last January, respectively.
